 Judgment

The 5th respondent in O.P.(M.V.) No.2526/ 2003 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Thrissur is the appellant herein.

(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal)
2.

The original petitioner filed the claim petition under Section 163A of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988, claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 15.05.2001.
In the accident, two vehicles were involved and the petitioner was the driver of a Tata Sumo.
The jeep bearing Reg No.TN- 21-Z-9084 hit against the Tata Sumo bearing Reg No.PY-1-J-4777 driven by the petitioner.
Respondent Nos.3, 4 and 5 are the owner, driver and insurer of the Jeep repectively.
The Tribunal awarded a compensation of Rs.65,920/- and directed the 5 th respondent to pay the same.
3. The insurance company filed a written statement, admitting the accident as well as policy, but disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

4. The evidence in the case consists of documentary evidence A1 toA9 and B1 to B4.
2025:KER:24553 MACA NO. 1489 OF 2014 5.
Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the 5th respondent preferred this appeal.

sentences.text:
Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?
7.

Heard Sri.Dinesh Mathew J. Muricken, the learned Counsel appearing for the appellant,
Sri.P.K.Chandra Mohan, the learned counsel for the 1st respondent and Sri.P.K.Manojkumar, the learned Standing Counsel.

8. According to the learned counsel for the appellant / 5th respondent, at the time of the accident the 4 th respondent, the driver of the Jeep had no valid driving license and therefore he seeks permission to recover the compensation from the 4 th respondent.
He has relied upon Ext.B4, copy of the driving license of the 5th respondent.
In this case, from the award it can be seen that respondent Nos. 1,3,4 and 5, have not filed any written statement.
Therefore, the 5th respondent cannot now contend that the 4th respondent had no valid driving license at the time of the accident.
From Ext.B4, which is a photo copy, it is not clear as to whether the 4th respondent had valid driving license at the time of the 2025:KER:24553 MACA NO. 1489 OF 2014 accident.
Since the 5th respondent had not filed any written statement disputing the driving licence of the driver, the prayer for the permission to recover the compensation from the insured is denied.
This MACA is dismissed.

Sd/-
C.PRATHEEP KUMAR JUDGE GBG The New India Assurance Co. Ltd vs Balasubrmanian on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32605769/
